planets.name: A Spanning Tree for Graph-RAG Traversal

manifest.title: A Spanning Tree for Graph-RAG Traversal
manifest.summary: Walk a cyclic knowledge graph naively and you get a broadcast storm — duplicate fetches, a context window full of repeats, a frontier that never converges. The Spanning Tree Protocol shows how to prune it.

planets.name: Agent Memory Is a Kalman Filter

manifest.title: Agent Memory Is a Kalman Filter
manifest.summary: Both maintain a belief about a hidden state from a stream of noisy inputs, and both do it the same way: **predict, then correct, weighting new evidence by how much you trust it.**

planets.name: Cognitive Biases Are Overfitting (Debiasing Is Regularization)

manifest.title: Cognitive Biases Are Overfitting (Debiasing Is Regularization)
manifest.summary: Most cognitive biases are the mind overfitting to a small, vivid sample: low "training error" (it feels obviously right from where you stand), high "test error" (it's wrong about the world), and a refusal to check the gap. That gap *is* high variance.

planets.name: Compression Is the Through-Line

manifest.title: Compression Is the Through-Line
manifest.summary: Intelligence and memory are both the art of packing more meaning into denser, retrievable representations. Learning ≈ compression.

planets.name: Directing Intelligence You Don't Own (Managing Up Is the AI-Steering Playbook)

manifest.title: Directing Intelligence You Don't Own (Managing Up Is the AI-Steering Playbook)
manifest.summary: Getting good outcomes from an agent more capable than you that you **cannot command, only orient** — that's the same problem whether the agent is a strong manager or a frontier model.

planets.name: FMEA Is the Rubric Pointed at Failure

manifest.title: FMEA Is the Rubric Pointed at Failure
manifest.summary: Severity and Occurrence are obvious. **Detection** is the sharp, transferable axis: a high-severity failure you can't *see coming* is worse than one you can, because you lose the chance to intervene.

planets.name: Goodhart's Law Is Overfitting (Every Scored System Needs a Holdout)

manifest.title: Goodhart's Law Is Overfitting (Every Scored System Needs a Holdout)
manifest.summary: Overfitting a backtest and gaming a scoring rubric are the *same* failure: you optimize a proxy until it stops predicting the reality it stood for.

planets.name: Grokking Is the Expertise Plateau

manifest.title: Grokking Is the Expertise Plateau
manifest.summary: The discouraging middle of any hard skill is diagnostic of progress, not its absence — it's the memorization phase that precedes the phase transition to true generalization.

planets.name: Pattern Recognition Needs a Holdout (Or It's Apophenia)

manifest.title: Pattern Recognition Needs a Holdout (Or It's Apophenia)
manifest.summary: "Get better at spotting patterns" and "stop seeing patterns that aren't there" are not two skills — they are precision and recall on the same detector.

planets.name: Production AI Is 10% Model, 90% Plumbing

manifest.title: Production AI Is 10% Model, 90% Plumbing
manifest.summary: Shipping AI is mostly engineering around the model, not the model itself. When evaluating a new AI feature, ask "where's the 90%?" first.

planets.name: RAG Searches Under the Streetlight (Coverage Is the Hidden Failure)

manifest.title: RAG Searches Under the Streetlight (Coverage Is the Hidden Failure)
manifest.summary: A retrieval system can only ever return answers from where the light is — the slice of the world that got chunked, embedded, and indexed. The danger is that the search feels exhaustive from inside the light.

planets.name: Sampling Beats the Lattice (Random Search Is Monte Carlo Over Configs)

manifest.title: Sampling Beats the Lattice (Random Search Is Monte Carlo Over Configs)
manifest.summary: Random hyperparameter search *is* Monte Carlo — uniform random sampling of a region you can't compute analytically, leaning on the law of large numbers.

planets.name: Subtraction Is Regularization (Fewer Parameters Generalize Better)

manifest.title: Subtraction Is Regularization (Fewer Parameters Generalize Better)
manifest.summary: Subtracting a feature or a commitment is regularization: fewer moving parts, lower variance (fragility), better generalization to the futures you didn't plan for.

planets.name: The Brain Is a Self-Improving Harness (Sparks Explore, Neurons Consolidate)

manifest.title: The Brain Is a Self-Improving Harness (Sparks Explore, Neurons Consolidate)
manifest.summary: A second brain isn't a notebook, or even a graph — it's a *harness that improves its own scaffolding*: explore cheaply, consolidate the best, and keep a human gate as the regularizer.

planets.name: The Fan-Out Port (Design as Spec, Parallel Porters, Build-Verify)

manifest.title: The Fan-Out Port (Design as Spec, Parallel Porters, Build-Verify)
manifest.summary: The quality comes from the **contract + the verify**, not from each agent being perfect. It turns "weeks of mechanical work" into one wall-clock pass.

planets.name: The Graph Compounds Like Interest

manifest.title: The Graph Compounds Like Interest
manifest.summary: A note that just sits there adds *principal*. A note that connects to many others earns on the *running total*. The value of a knowledge graph is the edge set, not the node count — and like compound interest, it goes slow-then-sudden.

planets.name: The Holdout Rule (Graded Systems Need Out-of-Sample)

manifest.title: The Holdout Rule (Graded Systems Need Out-of-Sample)
manifest.summary: Anything that grades against a metric needs a holdout — an out-of-sample check the optimizer never saw. It's the difference between a score that *looks* rigorous and one that *is*.

planets.name: The Rubric Pattern (Graded, Explainable AI Is the Trust Primitive)

manifest.title: The Rubric Pattern (Graded, Explainable AI Is the Trust Primitive)
manifest.summary: Intelligence is table stakes; trust is the product. The trust primitive is the rubric: a fixed, weighted, explainable scoring scheme graded against ground truth — never raw model output on faith.

planets.name: A Linked Vault Wants to Be a Graph RAG

manifest.title: A Linked Vault Wants to Be a Graph RAG
manifest.summary: A linked note vault is already a hand-built knowledge graph. Most graph-RAG systems build the graph *graph-last* by extraction; a curated vault was built *graph-first* by hand — and that inversion is the advantage.

planets.name: Wiki-Links Are DNS for the Vault

manifest.title: Wiki-Links Are DNS for the Vault
manifest.summary: If retrieval walks edges that don't resolve, the graph it traverses is a lie, and the answer inherits the lie.

planets.name: Behavioral Psychology — Product Applications

manifest.title: Behavioral Psychology — Product Applications
manifest.summary: Behavioral psychology is a design input: profile how people actually decide, then build the product around the real behavior, not the idealized one.

planets.name: Chirality Is Positioning

manifest.title: Chirality Is Positioning
manifest.summary: You don't always need new atoms (features). You need the mirror flip — the same molecule oriented so it reads as a different drug to the customer.

planets.name: Cold-Start Is a Change-Management Problem

manifest.title: Cold-Start Is a Change-Management Problem
manifest.summary: A two-sided marketplace cold-start is a population-level change-management problem — and the classic change playbook's eight steps map onto it almost line for line.

planets.name: Controlled Friction Builds Trust

manifest.title: Controlled Friction Builds Trust
manifest.summary: An adviser who agrees with everything has no credibility to spend. Planned, patterned friction signals that a position is real — and earns the trust that the eventual yes is worth.

planets.name: Cool Is a Requirement — iPod, Not Zune

manifest.title: Cool Is a Requirement — iPod, Not Zune
manifest.summary: Treat desirability as a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have. We want to be the iPod, not the Zune.

planets.name: Dijkstra to the Money Node

manifest.title: Dijkstra to the Money Node
manifest.summary: The right build order is literally Dijkstra's shortest path from "idea" to the first-dollar node. The prettiest feature is usually a high-weight edge that doesn't lie on that path — so the algorithm skips it.

planets.name: Idea to Revenue (A Validation Gate)

manifest.title: Idea to Revenue (A Validation Gate)
manifest.summary: Before building, make an idea pass a validation gate — and define how you'll kill it before you start.

planets.name: Model the Funnel as a One-Way State Machine

manifest.title: Model the Funnel as a One-Way State Machine
manifest.summary: Modeling a lifecycle as states + allowed transitions (not flags) makes illegal states unrepresentable.

planets.name: The Missing Money Node (Idea→Revenue Audit)

manifest.title: The Missing Money Node (Idea→Revenue Audit)
manifest.summary: A feature is only done when its conversion edge works end-to-end — no dead CTAs, no placeholder stubs, no gate that approves work but releases nothing. Every feature needs a working money node.

planets.name: Trojan-Horse GTM (The Free Wedge Sells the Case Study)

manifest.title: Trojan-Horse GTM (The Free Wedge Sells the Case Study)
manifest.summary: A deliberately-free pilot isn't a discount — it's a distribution buy. Its real deliverable isn't the work performed; it's the measured, quotable proof that unlocks the channel that scales.

planets.name: Virality, Distribution & the Rubric

manifest.title: Virality, Distribution & the Rubric
manifest.summary: Don't average your virality drivers — one fatal zero shouldn't hide behind four strong scores. And the content is only the 10%; distribution is the 90%.

planets.name: A Ranking Function for Trust (BM25 as a Reputation Engine)

manifest.title: A Ranking Function for Trust (BM25 as a Reputation Engine)
manifest.summary: A 40-year-old search-ranking formula already encodes the fairness rules a reputation score needs. A defensible score is a product's trust primitive — and BM25 supplies the math for one.

planets.name: Capacity-Aware Assignment (Round-Robin Is Naïve Staffing)

manifest.title: Capacity-Aware Assignment (Round-Robin Is Naïve Staffing)
manifest.summary: Round-robin only works when every server has identical capacity. The instant capacity is uneven, even distribution melts the weakest node while the strongest sits idle.

planets.name: 1:1s Are a Team's Heartbeat Protocol

manifest.title: 1:1s Are a Team's Heartbeat Protocol
manifest.summary: Liveness isn't a question you ask, it's a signal you monitor. Engagement is read from the cadence and texture of routine contact, not from asking "are you engaged?"

planets.name: Rumination Needs a Circuit Breaker

manifest.title: Rumination Needs a Circuit Breaker
manifest.summary: You don't stop a runaway by trying harder inside the loop — that *is* the retry storm. You stop it with an out-of-band trip that refuses to execute the loop body at all.

planets.name: Strengths Decay Like Moats

manifest.title: Strengths Decay Like Moats
manifest.summary: A personal strength is just a moat at the scale of one person — an edge relative to an environment. When the environment moves, an edge can flip into a liability.

planets.name: The Advisor as Servant-Leader

manifest.title: The Advisor as Servant-Leader
manifest.summary: "Disagrees sometimes" reads as a quirk; "serves your success, not your comfort" reads as a contract — a design constraint you can hold a transcript accountable to.

planets.name: A Backtest Is a Double Pendulum (Deterministic ≠ Predictable)

manifest.title: A Backtest Is a Double Pendulum (Deterministic ≠ Predictable)
manifest.summary: A strategy that survives only one trajectory has fit the chaos, not the signal. Data-snooping is just exploiting sensitive dependence — finding the one initial condition where the pendulum happened to swing your way.

planets.name: Curvature Is the Cost of Being Wrong

manifest.title: Curvature Is the Cost of Being Wrong
manifest.summary: Curvature is not geometry for its own sake; it is the **price of error per unit of deviation** — and the same quadratic form recurs across optimization, control, estimation, and portfolio risk.

planets.name: Feedback & Control (One Pattern, Four Domains)

manifest.title: Feedback & Control (One Pattern, Four Domains)
manifest.summary: The same abstract pattern — **negative feedback toward a setpoint** — hides in control theory, markets, biology, and AI agents. They're the same math wearing different clothes.

planets.name: Volatility Harvesting (Feedback Control You Want Disturbed)

manifest.title: Volatility Harvesting (Feedback Control You Want Disturbed)
manifest.summary: Turn the disturbance you'd normally fight into the thing you harvest. It's a design pattern, not just a trade.

planets.name: Clarity Is PCA for Priorities

manifest.title: Clarity Is PCA for Priorities
manifest.summary: "Clarity first, everything else second" is principal component analysis run on your to-do space: find the 1–2 axes that explain the most variance in outcomes, and discard the rest as noise.

planets.name: Run Attention Like a Leaky Bucket

manifest.title: Run Attention Like a Leaky Bucket
manifest.summary: The leaky-bucket rate limiter and most good time-management advice are the same control law applied to two overloaded servers — an API gateway and a human. Dropping is a feature, not a failure.

planets.name: The AI-Augmented Second Brain Stack

manifest.title: The AI-Augmented Second Brain Stack
manifest.summary: A second brain has three layers: a markdown-and-graph memory, AI agents as workers, and a loop where the system improves itself. The differentiator isn't the model — it's edge quality.

planets.name: The Barrier Is the Notation (Symbol Terror Is an Onboarding Tax)

manifest.title: The Barrier Is the Notation (Symbol Terror Is an Onboarding Tax)
manifest.summary: The blocker is never the idea, it's the **notation**. Good teaching pays the toll for the learner: translate the symbols first, then the idea arrives free.

planets.name: Mechanical Stress as Balanced Opposing Forces

manifest.title: Mechanical Stress as Balanced Opposing Forces
manifest.summary: "Balanced opposing forces about an equilibrium" is a portable mental model — it shows up in beams, control loops, markets, and homeostasis.

planets.name: Reusable Fixtures Are SpaceX Economics for Testing

manifest.title: Reusable Fixtures Are SpaceX Economics for Testing
manifest.summary: An expendable rocket is a fresh random dataset every test; a reusable booster is one deterministic generator flown a thousand times.

planets.name: Tesla-Valve the Workflow (Irreversibility by Construction)

manifest.title: Tesla-Valve the Workflow (Irreversibility by Construction)
manifest.summary: Irreversibility-by-construction beats irreversibility-by-policy the same way the Tesla valve beats a check valve with a spring: no part to fail.

planets.name: Throughput Comes From Removing Contention, Not From Tidiness

manifest.title: Throughput Comes From Removing Contention, Not From Tidiness
manifest.summary: A "tidy"-looking ordering optimizes for legibility, not throughput. Throughput is set by the *contended resource*.

planets.name: BI & Analysis Methodology

manifest.title: BI & Analysis Methodology
manifest.summary: Defensible methodology over clever shortcuts. An analysis you can't trace is an analysis you can't defend.

planets.name: Engine vs Rules (One Boundary, Three Jobs)

manifest.title: Engine vs Rules (One Boundary, Three Jobs)
manifest.summary: Draw the line between configurable Rules and the underlying Engine explicitly, once — and the ownership boundary, the multi-tenancy model, and the legal clarity all fall out for free.

planets.name: Sovereign AI Bottoms Out at the Power Meter

manifest.title: Sovereign AI Bottoms Out at the Power Meter
manifest.summary: Sovereignty over the AI stack doesn't close until it reaches the energy layer. It's a feasibility question, not an identity, and it lives in kWh/day.
